1

 Judgment
~~~~~~~~~ The appellant has invoked Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act in order to challenge the judgment dated 12.03.2019 in LAR No.2/2010 of the Sub Court, Neyyattinkara.
2. The land acquisition in question relates to 13.06 Ares of property in Survey No.681/15 of Vizhinjam Village.
The property was acquired by the State for the Tsunami Rehabilitation Project.
The Land Acquisition Officer fixed the land value at 45,698/- per Are.
Section 4(1) Notification is dated 11.04.2008.
Possession of the property was taken on 23.07.2009 and Award was passed on 15.12.2018.
3. The appellant preferred LAR No.2/2010 in the Sub Court, Neyyattinkara.

Before the Sub Court,
the appellant contended that the acquired property is an ideal residential- cum-agricultural land and there were high yielding coconut trees and other trees in the land at the time of acquisition.
The land is very near to Vizhinjam-Poovar public road and Vizhinjam-Balaramapuram public road.
The property is close to Kovalam, an International Tourist Centre.
4. The appellant contended that the Land Acquisition Officer did not consider the importance of locality and its proximity to private and public institutions while fixing the land value.
The potential value of the property was very high and it would have fetched at least 3 lakhs per Cent at the time of Section 4(1) Notification.
The compensation awarded was based on inclusion of the property in D Category.
The property ought to have been included at least in B Category.
The appellant prayed before the Sub Court that the land value may be refixed at 3 lakhs per Cent.
5. The respondent resisted the reference filing written statement.
The appellant/claimant has been given sufficient compensation, contended the respondent.
6. The Sub Court, after considering the evidence on record, rejected the claim of the appellant to fix enhanced land value based on Exts.A1, A4 and A5.
However, the Sub Court accepted the land value shown in Ext.A2 and fixed the market value at 53,599/- per Are (21,700/- per Cent).
The Sub Court awarded an enhanced market value of 1,03,184/-.
The Sub Court declared that the claimant is entitled to solatium at the rate of 30% on the enhanced marked value.

Interest at the rate of 12%
was awarded for the period from 02.06.2008 to 15.12.2008.

The appellant was also made entitled to interest at the rate of 9% per annum from 23.07.2009 to 22.07.2010 and thereafter with interest at the rate of 15% per annum till realisation from the respondents.
The appellant, dissatisfied by the judgment of the Sub Court, Neyyattinkara, has filed this Land Acquisition Appeal.
7. The appellant contended that the land is situated in a very important locality and was planted with high yielding coconut trees and other fruit bearing trees.
Apart from vibrant commercial institutions, there are also many governmental institutions nearby.
Therefore, the property in question will fetch at least a sum of 3 lakhs per Cent.
8. The appellant contended that the court below has clearly went wrong in discarding Ext.A4 document.
Post notification documents can also be accepted in evidence.

Ext.A1 judgment in LAR Jain Raj vs State Of Kerala on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52380015/
2 No.80/2005 is one passed by the Sub Court, Neyyattinkara.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no reason why Ext.A1 cannot be relied on.
The appellant pointed out that Ext.A4 document relates to a small extent of land and building and there is no evidence whatsoever to conclude that the value fixed in Ext.A4 is a fancy price.

The compensation allowed by the Sub Court, Neyyattinkara is therefore liable to be enhanced,
contended the counsel for the petitioner.
9. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader representing the respondent.
10. The acquisition relates to 13.06 Ares of land in Vizhinjam Village.
The Land Acquisition Officer fixed the land value at 45,698/- per Are.
In reference, the Sub Court, Neyyattinkara has enhanced the land value to 62,987/- per Are.
11. The appellant relied on Exts.A1, A2, A4 and A5 documents for enhancement of land value.

The market value was fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer based on a Sale Deed No.538/2007 of SRO,
Venganoor.
The said document is dated 05.03.2007.
The reference court found that there was a time lag of more than one year from the date of the document and Section 4(1) Notification.
The Sub Court therefore found that the market value ought to have been fixed at a higher rate giving an escalation of 10% at least.
12. As regards Ext.A4 Sale Deed, the Sub Court found that the Sale Deed related to 4.5 Ares of land along with a building.
The Reference Court held that Ext.A4 land being of a smaller extent with a building, such property will fetch more value compared to larger extent of land.
Ext.A4 document was therefore discarded.
I do not find any error in the conclusion arrived at by the Sub Court.

13. As regards Ext.A5 Sale Deed relied on by the appellant, the Reference Court found that the said sale is in respect of 2.717 Cents of property and was purchased for Vizhinjam International Port for a value of 2,45,000/- per Cent.

Ext .A5 was made after more than two years from Section 4(1)
Notification.

The Reference Court found that Ext.A5 need not be considered as there is already a comparable sale instance which took place around an year to Section 4(1) Notification.
14.
Section 4(1) Notification was on 11.04.2008.
The basic document relied on by the Land Acquisition Officer was dated 05.03.2007.
The Reference Court has enhanced the market value at a higher rate taking note of the fact that the basic document was executed more than one year before Section 4(1) Notification.
15. The Sub Court was right in rejecting the claim of the appellant based on Ext.A4 Sale Deed wherein the land value was 2,22,222/- per Are.
The said Ext.A4 property was in respect of a smaller extent of land (11.15 Cents) along with a building thereon.

The appellant, who is holding 13.06 Ares of property, without any building in the property, cannot aspire to get the value fixed in Ext.A4.
16.
As far as Ext.A5 Sale Deed is concerned, the said Sale Deed was executed on 13.09.2010 and is in respect of 2.717 Cents of land.
The value fixed was 2,45,000/- per Cent.

The market value was fixed Jain Raj vs State Of Kerala on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52380015/
3 by taking note of solatium and statutory interest.

entities.text: Jain Raj vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the circumstances, the Reference Court rightly refused to place reliance on Ext.A5.
17.
The appellant acquired the property as per Ext.A2 after Section 4(1) Notification.
The land value fixed in Ext.A2 was 53,599/- per Are.
The appellant has no case that the seller was related to him and Ext.A2 transaction was not in the course of ordinary sale.
In the facts of the case, the Reference Court was right in relying on the land value shown in Ext.A2, to fix the market value of the acquired property.
18. The Reference Court has granted enhanced market value of 1,03,184/- for the acquired property.
The appellant is made eligible for 30% solatium and has been granted 12% interest on the enhanced market value for the period from 02.06.2008 to 15.12.2008.
Interest has been awarded at the rate of 9% per annum from 23.07.2009 to 22.07.2010 and thereafter at the rate of 15% per annum till realisation of the enhanced compensation.
I do not find any reason to grant further enhancement of compensation.
The Land Acquisition Appeal is therefore dismissed.

Sd/-
 N. NAGARESH, JUDGE aks PETITIONER'S ANNEXURES Annexure-I
